title: Condon as musical director and organizer
summary: He defends Condon as a real organizer who knew which men to put together and whom the band worked hard for, calling himself the social director.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: No he never no - no. But, that was one of the things I think some of the records that were made in that period of time, you know, I did a lot of things with Jack Teagarden - you know - such wonderful things; I did a lot of things with Gene Krupa where they used most of the Condon Band and that kind of stuff. And, Eddie was usually in on all that as well - you know - playing his guitar.
This would be a good opportunity to say in making those records was Condon basically the musical director?

He was very good - himself - he was very good at mapping stuff out and he was a marvelous organizer and he knew the right guys to put together; that's half of the battle and don't forget he surrounded himself with the right guys.
And, he always had a good band behind him. Of course, when you got a club like that, you know, you have a choice on your own.
But, you give him full credit for what he did - there wasn't any fluke.
A lot of people said that Condon was just a front man and didn't know what he was doing and---
You're saying there was substance to the man---

Listen, I think that many people that came to Condon's would give a damn sight rather have him at the table telling his funny jokes than having him up on the bandstand and he used to call himself The Social Director---
But, he was also the musical director when he was in good shape - you said---
Oh, sure. How do you think we all hung together. We all were behind him. I mean, we all worked hard for him; he was lucky that he had a band that worked---
Yeah because everybody had a great amount of respect for Eddie - you know.
